name: The Vaultwalkers (Sealed Shelf Infrastructure Urbex)
description: Where the Carcass Tours focus on Old Chicago ruins, the Vaultwalkers specialize in the sealed, still-pressurized infrastructure beneath the Shelf — service corridors, emergency shelters, and water management vaults that were locked down during the 2194 Shelf Compaction and never reopened. Entry requires defeating active (if aging) corporate security systems, and several corridors still contain functional automated maintenance drones that have been operating on loop programs for nearly thirty years. The community is small, technically skilled, and fiercely private; membership is by introduction only, and the Vaultwalkers share maps exclusively through physical dead drops rather than any digital medium. Their most celebrated discovery, in 2221, was a fully intact Kurosawa-Petrov emergency operations center sealed since 2195 — still powered, still logging data, its logs containing records the corponation has publicly claimed do not exist.
cultural_impact: The Vaultwalkers have quietly become an informal intelligence network for Shelf communities, and the physical dead-drop communication model they pioneered has been adopted by multiple unrelated underground organizations as a counter-surveillance practice.
key_figures: A maintenance drone designated Unit 7-Pale (semi-adopted mascot)
locations: Sealed Shelf service corridor network, Sub-Level 4
The Compaction Seam (boundary of the 2194 lockdown zone)
story_hooks: The Kurosawa-Petrov operations center logs contain evidence of a 2195 event the corponation has spent thirty years erasing — and the corponation has just learned the Vaultwalkers found the site.
A Vaultwalker goes missing in a section of the sealed corridors that no member has ever returned from, and the community must decide whether to mount a rescue or protect their secrecy.
A new member introduced through a trusted contact is feeding location data to a corporate security contractor — but they have their own reasons for infiltrating, and they're not what anyone assumes.
